Variants.Content: Bear Island is located in the cold sea northwest of the North. It is the island where the Mormont family has lived. The land on the island is not abundant, and wind is more common than wheat; residents rely on fishing, hunting, timber, sea animals, and hard farming to survive, so both men and women are accustomed to working, holding arms, and watching the sea. The people of Bear Island are famous for not giving in to hardship. This is not a simple heroic legend, but a skill forced by life on an isolated island: winter comes early, shipping schedules are uncertain, and foreign predators are more likely to appear than southern merchants. The island has a vassal relationship with the north, but retains a strong independent temperament.

Entry Bear Island A stronghold was therefore not just a lord's hall, but also a place where weddings and funerals, vows, labor and local memories recurred.

Entry Bear Island They care about firewood, hunting grounds, peat, salt fish, and granaries that can survive the long winter. They also care about whether seeds are left after the grain collection and whether the city gates are open in times of disaster. When people from afar see coats of arms, they see whether there will be food to eat tomorrow.
